captions.detailed: A rangefinder binocular featuring a wide, split rectangular body housing two main objective barrels. It is designed with a central revolute hinge for interpupillary distance adjustment, a large ridged focus wheel situated on top, and a small mode selector dial on the right body housing. The entire assembly is constructed from matte black plastic, with blue-tinted optical glass lenses visible at the front of the barrels.
captions.instruction: Generate a CadQuery model of a rangefinder binocular. It should feature two main body halves connected by a central hinge joint, a top-mounted cylindrical focus wheel that rotates, and a smaller mode selector dial on one of the body housings, all finished in a dark matte material.
captions.factory: The model is built from several parts. The left and right body housings are constructed using Box primitives, filleted on their vertical edges, with cylindrical protrusions representing the objective and eyepiece barrels. A central hinge uses concentric cylinders to link the left and right assemblies with a revolute joint. The top focus wheel is created by patterning small rectangular ribs around a central Cylinder and is attached via a revolute joint. The mode dial is a small cylinder with a rectangular indicator bar, mounted to the right housing with another revolute joint.
